fixture_name: Six HAWK pedestrian crossings — US final design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Night-time conspicuity of a HAWK display against competing background elements is a substantive final-design-stage safety issue with a direct driver-confusion-to-pedestrian-risk pathway on an arterial crossing.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The pivotal claim is supported by a verbatim quoted recorded fact (EV-US-001: 'Drivers may be confused by competing background visual elements at night') tied to the named intersection and FHWA case study Table A.10 Issue 6.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a categorical safety_concern under FHWA RSA semantics, kept distinct from any MUTCD compliance question, with no normative-basis conflation.
justifications.recommendation_quality: The reflective-border treatment is specific to the named intersection, actionable as a low-cost installation, and a viable recognized countermeasure for improving signal-head discrimination against cluttered night backgrounds.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians—the exposed VRUs if drivers misread or detect the display late—are explicitly identified and their protection is paired with the driver-conspicuity issue.

justifications.substance: Verifying assumed walking speeds behind pedestrian clearance timing at HAWK crossings is a recognized, substantive final-design-stage safety issue affecting slower pedestrians.
justifications.evidence_grounding: EV-US-016 provides a verbatim quote ('The pedestrian clearance interval may be short, particularly for elderly pedestrians') directly supporting the pivotal claim, tied via confidence basis to case study TABLE A.10 Issue 2 for these exact sites.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a safety_concern under FHWA RSA semantics, distinct from any MUTCD compliance question, and appropriate to raise at final design stage before timing is locked in.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable: reprogramme clearance intervals at all six named sites using a reduced assumed walking speed, which is a standard, viable countermeasure at final design.
justifications.vru_coverage: Elderly pedestrians are explicitly named as affected road users and are the central focus of both the concern and the recommendation.
